questions.title: Why do we dream?
questions.fact: Most vivid dreams happen in REM sleep, when your brain is almost as active as when you're awake.

questions.title: What's at the bottom of the ocean?
questions.fact: Most of the ocean floor has never been mapped in detail.

questions.title: Is there life on other planets?
questions.fact: Astronomers have confirmed more than 5,000 planets orbiting other stars.

questions.title: Who decides what counts as a crime?
questions.fact: The age of criminal responsibility is 10 in England and Wales, and 12 in Scotland.

questions.title: What did people eat 2,000 years ago?
questions.fact: Romans splashed a fermented fish sauce called garum on their food, a bit like ketchup.

questions.title: Why are some countries rich and others poor?
questions.fact: The 2024 Nobel Prize in economics went to research on exactly this question.

questions.title: How does a virus spread?
questions.fact: A single sneeze can send droplets several metres across a room.

questions.title: Can a computer be creative?
questions.fact: In 2018 a portrait made by an AI sold at Christie's for $432,500.

questions.title: What makes a song catchy?
questions.fact: Researchers call a song stuck in your head an "earworm", and study why it happens.

questions.title: How do you design a city people love?
questions.fact: Manhattan's street grid was planned in 1811, long before most of it was built.

questions.title: Is it ever right to break a rule?
questions.fact: Philosophers have argued over the "trolley problem" since 1967.

questions.title: How do bees find their way home?
questions.fact: Honeybees tell each other where food is by doing a "waggle dance".

questions.title: What keeps a skyscraper up in an earthquake?
questions.fact: Some skyscrapers hide giant swinging weights inside to stop them swaying.

questions.title: Why do people believe fake news?
questions.fact: A 2018 MIT study found false news spread faster on Twitter than true news.

questions.title: Can we save a species on the brink?
questions.fact: Humpback whales were hunted close to extinction. Many populations have since recovered.
